speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a pediatric patient presenting with systemic hypertension; to begin our evaluation, how old are you and do you have a family history of high blood pressure or kidney disease?

speaker: Patient
text: 5-year-old boy. The patient is presented by his mother for a well-child visit. The boy was born at 39 weeks gestation via spontaneous vaginal delivery, is currently up to date on all vaccines, and is meeting all developmental milestones. His mother reports that he has been generally doing well with no concerns. No family history of cardiovascular disease. The boy does not take any medications.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for that information. Since this is a well-child visit in a 5-year-old with no family history, I need to determine if this hypertension is primary or secondary. Do you notice any symptoms like headaches, blurred vision, vomiting, or swelling in his legs or around his eyes?

REQUEST TEST: Basic_Metabolic_Panel, Urinalysis
REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal_Ultrasound

speaker: Doctor
text: The measurements show normal readings, which is unexpected given the presentation of systemic hypertension. Let's focus on the physical exam and urine findings: Do you notice any swelling in his face, legs, or around his eyes? Also, did the Urinalysis report any protein or blood, and what do the abdominal ultrasound images show regarding the kidneys?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is High blood pressure on the right upper extremity.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That is a very important finding. Hypertension isolated to the right upper extremity strongly suggests a mechanical obstruction of blood flow, such as a coarctation of the aorta. Can you tell me if you have noticed cold feet, weak pulses in your legs, or any pain when walking?

REQUEST TEST: Upper and Lower Extremity Blood Pressure Measurement, ECG
REQUEST IMAGES: Chest_X-Ray

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Blood_Pressure_Right_Upper_Extremity: 150/80 mm Hg; Precordial_Auscultation: Normal S1 and S2, 2/6 long systolic murmur with systolic ejection click over the left sternal border and back; Echocardiogram_Findings: Narrowing of the aorta distal to the left subclavian artery with a gradient, consistent with coarctation. Left ventricular function is normal; Blood_Pressure_Differential_Upper_Extremities: 150/80 mm Hg (Right), Compared to lower values in lower extremities; Chest_X-ray_Findings: Normal heart size, rib notching not observed (may not be present in young children).

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Coarctation of the Aorta. The clinical presentation of hypertension in the right upper extremity combined with a blood pressure differential between arms and legs, a systolic murmur, and echocardiographic confirmation of aortic narrowing is definitive for this condition.
